Based on the indexed codebase analysis, I cannot verify the merge readiness. Here's my assessment:

**Observable facts:**
- system_v5: 16,773 functions across clustered modules (cohesion 0.887)
- system_v7: Additional ~7,500+ functions (102-member cluster, cohesion 0.846)
- High-complexity hotspots: 3,806 functions with transitive loop depth ≥5 (max depth: 15)
- Touched files: 492 (~12.4% of v5/v7 codebase)
- Multiple interdependent systems (v4–v8 call graph)

**Critical blockers:**
1. Cannot access git worktree state, commit DAG, or merge conflict status
2. Cannot verify that 43 commits across 10 worktrees have been tested together
3. Cannot confirm pre-merge verification (test results, integration test runs)
4. No visibility into which files were actually modified (cannot distinguish code, config, docs changes)

**Risk surface:**
- Multi-system changes with tight cohesion (0.84–0.89) suggest tightly coupled logic
- High complexity concentration (15-level nesting) makes blind merges risky
- Parallel worktrees may contain overlapping changes to the same modules
